subject: Lighthouse Retail - pricing slab, PO field constraints & invoice cadence
messages:
From: Asha Menon <asha.menon@lighthouse-retail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lighthouse-retail.com
Date: 2027-05-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: Lighthouse Retail procurement: PO fields, net90 request and consolidated invoicing

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the product overview last week — Lighthouse Retail is excited about the potential. Procurement has a few requirements we need baked into contracting and billing before we can proceed to PO issuance:

- We require a PO number on each invoice and the PO should map to a single legal entity (we have three billing entities; we will indicate which one to use).
- Our standard payment term is Net 90. Please confirm whether Redwood can support Net 90 on this engagement or offer an alternative cadence.
- We ask for consolidated monthly statements rather than itemized weekly invoices for large SaaS partners. Would Redwood accept a monthly consolidated invoice for all committed spend?
- We may split payment across two POs if required by our treasury process — please confirm whether partial invoices referencing different POs are acceptable.

I've attached our PO template and procurement checklist. If these constraints are deal-breakers, let me know quickly; otherwise we will prepare a PO contingent on finalizing commercial terms.

Regards,
Asha Menon
Head of Procurement, Lighthouse Retail
asha.menon@lighthouse-retail.com
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Lighthouse_PO_Template_v2.xlsx, procurement-checklist.pdf

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Menon <asha.menon@lighthouse-retail.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-07T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Lighthouse Retail procurement: PO fields, net90 request and consolidated invoicing

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear list and for the template. Looping in Vanessa (finance) to confirm the billing mechanics. Quick responses inline below.

- PO number on each invoice: Yes, we can include your PO on every invoice. We also support a PO → legal-entity mapping in our billing system; we'll need the exact entity name and tax ID to route correctly.

- Net 90: We typically price around Net 30/45. Net 90 is longer than standard for new customers, but we can consider it for Lighthouse if we (a) agree a phased payment schedule and (b) include a small payment-processing uplift / credit holdback for extended terms. Vanessa, can you confirm what uplift range we'd need to protect against extended receivables?

- Consolidated monthly statements: We support monthly consolidated statements for committed spend. If Lighthouse prefers a single monthly statement that aggregates all invoices across POs for that entity, that's doable — we just need to know the reporting layout you require.

- Split payment across two POs / partial invoices: Our billing engine supports partial invoices referencing different PO numbers as long as we have a mapping upfront. We do prefer to avoid more than three split-POs per legal entity per month due to reconciliation overhead.

I'll prepare a short matrix showing options (Net term vs uplift, invoice cadence, PO-splitting rules) and attach the draft.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood-Pricing-Slabs-2027Q2.pdf

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Asha Menon <asha.menon@lighthouse-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-08T08:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Lighthouse Retail procurement: PO fields, net90 request and consolidated invoicing

Hi Asha, Jonas — Vanessa from Finance here. Thank you for the details, Asha. A few clarifications and Redwood constraints from the finance side: 

1) Net 90 consideration: For Net 90 we'd typically require either (i) a 2% billing uplift (applied to invoice face value) or (ii) a 30% initial prepayment held against commitments, released monthly as invoices clear. The uplift helps cover DSO risk. Either option is acceptable to Redwood and negotiable by deal size.

2) PO-to-entity mapping: Provide full legal entity name + tax ID and we will ensure the ACH wire / remit address and invoice header align. We cannot accept ambiguous entity mapping.

3) Consolidated monthly statement: We can issue one PDF statement per legal entity per month that aggregates activity across POs. However, our AR team still issues supporting invoice line-item PDFs (one per invoice) for your AP system. If you need only one document, we can include the line items in the consolidated PDF with per-invoice subtotals.

4) Split payments across two POs: We can accept split payments but we prefer all splits to be declared prior to the first invoice run. Reconciliations beyond two POs per month will trigger a manual review and may delay payments.

Ben will provide suggested wording for the SOW/addendum to capture the uplift or prepayment structure.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Finance Ops, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

---
Attachment referenced: Master_SOW_v3.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Menon <asha.menon@lighthouse-retail.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-08T15:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Lighthouse Retail procurement: PO fields, net90 request and consolidated invoicing

Asha — following Vanessa's options, here's a compact proposal that tends to work well operationally and satisfies procurement teams: 

Option A (preferred for low friction):
- Net 45 payment term (compromise).
- 1% uplift on invoices if Lighthouse needs Net 45 instead of our standard Net 30.
- Monthly consolidated statement + per-invoice PDF attachments for AP.
- Up to 2 POs per legal entity per month allowed; additional splits require pre-approval and may add a fixed reconciliation fee of $150 per extra PO.

Option B (if Lighthouse requires Net 90):
- Net 90 with 2% uplift OR 25% initial prepayment (applied to first invoice run and held as credit).
- Monthly consolidated statement as above.
- PO mapping required up front; we will not accept changes to PO → entity mapping mid-month.

Please confirm which option you prefer and provide the legal entity name/tax ID to seed billing. If you prefer, we can draft a short revenue addendum that codifies the uplift and PO-splitting rules so your legal and procurement teams can sign quickly.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Billing Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 650-555-0122

Attachment: proposed-addendum-draft.docx

From: Asha Menon <asha.menon@lighthouse-retail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Lighthouse Retail procurement: PO fields, net90 request and consolidated invoicing

Thanks, team — appreciate the clear options. Lighthouse reviews these internally and prefers to proceed with Option A (Net 45 + 1% uplift) to avoid prepayment.

Action items from our side:
- I'll send the full legal entity name and tax ID by EOD (please hold the PO mapping until you receive this).
- We will submit two POs initially (one for core platform committed capacity, one for professional services ramp). If we need additional POs later we will flag them during the monthly billing window.
- Please send the short revenue addendum and a sample consolidated statement layout so our AP can validate it against our ERP ingestion.

If you can send the addendum draft and the sample PDF by COB today, procurement can prepare the POs for signature.

Regards,
Asha Menon
Head of Procurement, Lighthouse Retail
